A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PhysioWave research. All pages, including Appendices A-F, support comparison through readable text and rendered figures. The original material can be matched reliably across the appendix expansion.

before.justification: Sections 3.2-3.3 report original ECG, EMG and multimodal classification results and ablations. Appendix E also reports signal-reconstruction outcomes.

after.justification: The original empirical results remain, supplemented by EPN612 class-level performance, confusion matrices and learned-feature visualizations in Appendix E.2.

M1.justification: Section 2 and Algorithm 1 retain the same wavelet decomposition, adaptive gating, cross-scale fusion, frequency-guided masking, reconstruction objective and downstream procedures. The added feature visualizations introduce no method component.

E1.justification: The pretraining corpora and downstream datasets in Tables 7-9 are unchanged. EPN612 in the new appendix is the existing EPN-612 benchmark, whose five active gestures and relaxed-hand class were already described in Appendix D.2.

E2.justification: Tables 1-2 and Figures 5-6 retain their comparator sets, including Moment and OTiS for EMG. The added embedding projections analyze the proposed model's features; the ROC chance diagonal is a reference rather than an evaluated competing model.

E3.justification: Appendix E.2 extends EPN612 evaluation with per-class precision, recall, F1 and ROC-AUC, plus PCA, t-SNE and UMAP analyses. Existing subject-wise 6:2:2 splits, preprocessing, model configurations and training budgets retain their previous specifications.

E4.justification: Appendix E.2 adds substantial analyses of which gestures are confused and how learned representations separate classes, using class-level diagnostics and three embedding projections. These questions extend the retained masking/pretraining ablation and reconstruction visualizations.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests. The new class-level plots remain point estimates, and multiple viewing angles are not independent experimental repetitions.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark and ablation values are unchanged. Appendix E.2 adds EPN612 confusion counts, AUCs of 0.981-0.999, and class-level scores including F1 of 0.883 for open and 0.996 for noGesture. The model size is unspecified, preventing direct attribution to a Small, Base or Large result.

T1.justification: Equations 1-15 and Algorithm 1 are unchanged. The new dimensionality-reduction discussion supplies conceptual explanations without new mathematical definitions, assumptions, derivations or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about wavelet-based representation learning, pretrained EMG/ECG models and multimodal fusion. The appendix adds supporting analyses without redefining these contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix E.2 newly interprets errors among similar dynamic gestures, identifies difficulty detecting open, and argues that embedding patterns demonstrate separability and spatially robust clustering. Appendix F's existing modality and generalization limitations are unchanged and merely relocated.

D1.justification: Figure 11 newly discloses per-class test supports of 1,224 or 1,071 examples, and Appendix E.2 specifies projection methods and viewing angles. This does not establish changed sample sizes. Existing implementation, hyperparameter, hardware and access information remains unchanged.

R1.justification: The bibliography and Appendix A are unchanged. No cited work is added or removed, and the paper's novelty claims and positioning relative to previous research remain the same.

P1.justification: V2 adds an acknowledgment section and reorganizes Appendix E into retained pretraining visualizations and a new EPN612 subsection with explanatory prose. The main narrative is unchanged, and the limitations text moves intact.

P2.justification: Figures 9-14 introduce a substantial visual-analysis extension: a confusion matrix, ROC curves, grouped class metrics and multi-view PCA, t-SNE and UMAP panels. Existing Figures 1-8 and Tables 1-9 are retained; the expanded appendix relocates the limitations section.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's aggregate EPN612 reporting, Appendix E.2 provides useful class-specific diagnostics, particularly open's 87.4% recall and common confusions. This modestly improves transparency. The gain is limited by unclear linkage to the model sizes in Table 2 and cluster-separation claims stronger than the overlapping patterns in Figures 12-14 demonstrate.
